card.name: Ghoomar
card.era: Bhil tribal origins, later adopted by Rajputs
card.tagline: Rajasthani twirling veil-and-ghaghara women's folk dance
card.profile: Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan originally performed by the Bhil tribe to worship the goddess Saraswati and later embraced by Rajput communities (Wikipedia). Chiefly performed by veiled women in flowing skirts (ghaghara), dancers pirouette while moving in and out of a wide circle; the word derives from 'ghoomna', meaning twirling (Wikipedia). Newly married brides are traditionally expected to dance ghoomar when welcomed to their marital home, and it features at weddings, Teej and religious occasions, with regional variations across Udaipur, Jodhpur and Kota-Bundi (Pratha).
card.insight: Ghoomar reached wide modern visibility through the song 'Ghoomar' in the 2017 Bollywood film Padmaavat, and the Gangaur Ghoomar Dance Academy was founded by Rajmata Goverdhan Kumari in 1986 to preserve the form (Wikipedia).

parts.note: Introduction and welcome to part 3 of the Rajasthani dance tutorial series.
Detailed step-by-step instruction of 10 basic hand steps for Rajasthani and Ghoomar dance.

steps.name: Step 1
steps.description: Fingers joined together, moving right and left while gliding downwards.

steps.name: Step 2
steps.description: Twisting hands and touching the opposite shoulder alternately.

steps.name: Step 3
steps.description: Creating an L-shape with arms and waving while moving side to side.

steps.name: Step 4
steps.description: Twisting both hands outward as if lifting a veil from the face.

steps.name: Step 5
steps.description: Crossing hands in a diagonal path and touching shoulders.

steps.name: Step 6
steps.description: Swaying hands smoothly from side to side with joined fingers.

lessons.teacher_style: The instructor patiently guides viewers through foundational Rajasthani hand movements with clear verbal breakdowns. She demonstrates each step at a measured tempo from a frontal perspective.
lessons.distinctive_method: Focuses exclusively on hand and arm placements across multiple progressive steps before combining them with music.
what_works: Step-by-step numerical counting helps follow the rhythm easily.
Clear visual demonstrations of hand placements and postures.
what_hinders: The dancer's face is covered by a veil, which obscures facial expressions.
